items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to enacting the "state workforce injury reduction act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6464

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to enacting the
"state workforce injury reduction act"

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To ensure that agencies seriously examine injuries to their employees
and formulate ways to prevent similar injuries from occurring in the
future.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill names the act the "state workforce injury
reduction act".

Section 2 of the bill amends section 7 of the civil service law by
adding a new subdivision 7 that requires each state agency referenced
in the annual report issued by the president of the civil service
commission pursuant to this section to write and submit an action plan
with participation from employee representatives for reducing
occurrences of such injuries in the coming year.

Section 3 requires the act to take effect immediately.

 DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE) :

Section 7 of the civil service law is amended by adding a new
subdivision, subdivision 7, that increases the required period that a
report is issued from annually, to every other year. It also increases
the time that the report can be acted upon.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently the president of the New York State Department of Civil
Service produces an annual report describing occupational injuries,
illnesses, and workers' compensation claims for each state agency.
However, there is no requirement that agencies respond to the report
with a plan for reducing the kinds of injuries identified in the
report. This legislation would ensure that agencies work with employee
representatives to seriously examine injuries to their employees and
formulate ways to prevent similar injuries from occurring in the
future.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S. 2842A - Vetoed - Veto Memo
 267

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

Minimal costs, but less worker compensation claims as a result of the
passage of this legislation will result in savings to Hew York State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 315
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 6464-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to enacting the
      state workforce injury reduction act"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would require all agencies listed in the Department of Civil
Service's (DCS) annual Accident Reporting System (ARS) report to  submit
a written action plan aimed at reducing the occurrence of injuries iden-
tified in the ARS in the upcoming year. State agencies would be required
to involve employee collective bargaining units in preparation of action
plans.  This  bill  would  also require DCS to issue, within 240 days of
publication, an addendum to the ARS report that contains  a  summary  of
each agency's action plan.
 
  I  previously  vetoed a similar version of this bill in 2016. My prior
concerns remain. This bill is unnecessary, as it would require  agencies
to address issues that are already being managed at an enterprise level.
The  State  has  created an Enterprise Risk Management program to proac-
tively and comprehensively reduce work place  hazards,  reduce  employee
fraud  and  abuse, better manage an injured worker's compensation claim,
and reduce the State's workers' compensation costs. Additionally,  agen-
cies currently do not have the trained staff needed to prepare or imple-
ment the action plans mandated by this bill.
 
  While the intent of this bill is laudable, the bill would mandate that
agencies  focus their limited resources on one aspect of risk management
to the detriment of more comprehensive and effective strategies that are
being developed and tested. Accordingly, I am constrained to  veto  this
bill.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
